overview:
This check monitors [IBM Websphere Application Server (WAS)][1] through the Datadog Agent. This check supports IBM WAS versions >= 8.5.5.

**Minimum Agent version:** 6.10.0

[1]: https://www.ibm.com/cloud/websphere-application-platform
setup:
Follow the instructions below to install and configure this check for an Agent running on a host. For containerized environments, see the [Autodiscovery Integration Templates][2] for guidance on applying these instructions.

The IBM WAS Datadog integration collects enabled PMI Counters from the WebSphere Application Server environment. Setup requires enabling the PerfServlet, which provides a way for Datadog to retrieve performance data from WAS.

By default, this check collects JDBC, JVM, thread pool, and Servlet Session Manager metrics. You may optionally specify additional metrics to collect in the "custom_queries" section. See the [sample check configuration][3] for examples.

### Installation

The IBM WAS check is included in the [Datadog Agent][4] package.

#### Enable the `PerfServlet`

The servlet's .ear file (PerfServletApp.ear) is located in the `<WAS_HOME>/installableApps` directory, where `<WAS_HOME>` is the installation path for WebSphere Application Server.

The performance servlet is deployed exactly as any other servlet. Deploy the servlet on a single application server instance within the domain.

**Note**: Starting with version 6.1, you must enable application security to get the PerfServlet working.

### Modify the monitored statistic set

By default, your application server is only configured for "Basic" monitoring. To gain visibility into your JVM, JDBC connections, and servlet connections, change the monitored statistic set for your application server from "Basic" to "All".

From the Websphere Administration Console, you can find this setting in `Application servers > <YOUR_APP_SERVER> > Performance Monitoring Infrastructure (PMI)`.

Once you've made this change, click "Apply" to save the configuration and restart your application server. Additional JDBC, JVM, and servlet metrics should appear in Datadog shortly after this change.

### Configuration

#### Prepare IBM WAS

As a best practice, Datadog recommends using a read-only user to monitor your IBM WAS instance. This limits the access granted to the Datadog Agent.

<!-- xxx tabs xxx -->
<!-- xxx tab "Host" xxx -->

#### Host

To configure this check for an Agent running on a host:

##### Metric collection

1. Edit the `ibm_was.d/conf.yaml` file, in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your Agent's configuration directory to collect your IBM WAS performance data. See the [sample ibm_was.d/conf.yaml][3] for all available configuration options.

2. [Restart the Agent][5].

##### Log collection

_Available for Agent versions >6.0_

1. Collecting logs is disabled by default in the Datadog Agent, enable it in your `datadog.yaml` file:

   ```yaml
   logs_enabled: true
   ```

2. Next, edit `ibm_was.d/conf.yaml` by uncommenting the `logs` lines at the bottom. Update the logs `path` with the correct path to your WAS log files.

   ```yaml
   logs:
     - type: file
       path: /opt/IBM/WebSphere/AppServer/profiles/InfoSphere/logs/server1/*.log
       source: ibm_was
       service: websphere
   ```

3. [Restart the Agent][5].

<!-- xxz tab xxx -->
<!-- xxx tab "Containerized" xxx -->

#### Containerized

For containerized environments, see the [Autodiscovery Integration Templates][2] for guidance on applying the parameters below.

##### Metric collection

| Parameter            | Value                                                                         |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<INTEGRATION_NAME>` | `ibm_was`                                                                     |
| `<INIT_CONFIG>`      | blank or `{}`                                                                 |
| `<INSTANCE_CONFIG>`  | `{"servlet_url": "http://%%host%%:%%port%%/wasPerfTool/servlet/perfservlet"}` |

##### Log collection

_Available for Agent versions >6.0_

Collecting logs is disabled by default in the Datadog Agent. To enable it, see [Kubernetes Log Collection][6].

| Parameter      | Value                                                |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `<LOG_CONFIG>` | `{"source": "ibm_was", "service": "<SERVICE_NAME>"}` |

<!-- xxz tab xxx -->
<!-- xxz tabs xxx -->

### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][7] and look for `ibm_was` under the Checks section.

[3]: https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/ibm_was/datadog_checks/ibm_was/data/conf.yaml.example
[4]: /account/settings/agent/latest
[5]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/agent/guide/agent-commands/#start-stop-and-restart-the-agent
[6]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/agent/kubernetes/log/
[7]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/agent/guide/agent-commands/#agent-status-and-information

metrics.name: ibm_was.can_connect
metrics.description: The ability of the integration to connect to the Perf Servlet to collect metrics

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.allocate_count
metrics.description: The total number of managed connections that were allocated since pool creation.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.close_count
metrics.description: The total number of managed connections that were destroyed since pool creation.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.connection_handle_count
metrics.description: The number of connections that are in use. Can include multiple connections that are shared from a single managed connection.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.create_count
metrics.description: The total number of managed connections that were created since pool creation.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.fault_count
metrics.description: The total number of faults, such as timeouts, in the connection pool.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.free_pool_size
metrics.description: The number of managed connections that are in the free pool.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.jdbc_time
metrics.description: The average time in milliseconds spent running in the JDBC driver that includes time that is spent in the JDBC driver, network, and database.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.managed_connection_count
metrics.description: The total number of managed connections in the free, shared, and unshared pools.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.percent_maxed
metrics.description: The percent of the time that all connections are in use.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.percent_used
metrics.description: The percent of the pool that is in use.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.pool_size
metrics.description: The size of the connection pool.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.prep_stmt_cache_discard_count
metrics.description: The total number of statements that are discarded by the least recently used (LRU) algorithm of the statement cache.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.return_count
metrics.description: The total number of managed connections that were returned since pool creation.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.use_time
metrics.description: The average time in milliseconds that a connection is in use.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.wait_time
metrics.description: The average waiting time in milliseconds until a connection is granted if a connection is not currently available.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jdbc.waiting_thread_count
metrics.description: The number of threads that are currently waiting for a connection.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jvm.free_memory
metrics.description: Deprecated, use ibm_was.jvm.free_memory_gauge instead

metrics.name: ibm_was.jvm.free_memory_gauge
metrics.description: The free memory in the JVM run time

metrics.name: ibm_was.jvm.heap_size
metrics.description: Deprecated, use ibm_was.jvm.heap_size_gauge instead

metrics.name: ibm_was.jvm.heap_size_gauge
metrics.description: The total memory in the JVM run time

metrics.name: ibm_was.jvm.process_cpu_usage
metrics.description: Deprecated, use ibm_was.jvm.process_cpu_usage_gauge instead

metrics.name: ibm_was.jvm.process_cpu_usage_gauge
metrics.description: The CPU Usage (in percent) of the Java virtual machine.

metrics.name: ibm_was.jvm.up_time
metrics.description: Deprecated, use ibm_was.jvm.up_time_gauge instead

metrics.name: ibm_was.jvm.up_time_gauge
metrics.description: The amount of time that the JVM is running

metrics.name: ibm_was.jvm.used_memory
metrics.description: Deprecated, use ibm_was.jvm.used_memory_gauge instead

metrics.name: ibm_was.jvm.used_memory_gauge
metrics.description: The used memory in the JVM run time

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.activate_non_exist_session_count
metrics.description: The number of requests for a session that no longer exists, presumably because the session timed out. Use this counter to help determine if the timeout is too short.

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.active_count
metrics.description: The number of concurrently active sessions. A session is active if the WebSphere Application Server is currently processing a request that uses that session.

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.affinity_break_count
metrics.description: The number of requests that are received for sessions that were last accessed from another web application. This value can indicate failover processing or a corrupt plug-in configuration.

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.cache_discard_count
metrics.description: The number of session objects that have been forced out of the cache. A least recently used (LRU) algorithm removes old entries to make room for new sessions and cache misses. Applicable only for persistent sessions.

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.create_count
metrics.description: The number of sessions that were created

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.external_read_size
metrics.description: Size of the session data read from persistent store. Applicable only for (serialized) persistent sessions; similar to external Read Time.

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.external_read_time
metrics.description: The time (ms) taken in reading the session data from the persistent store. For multirow sessions, the metrics are for the attribute; for single row sessions, the metrics are for the entire session. Applicable only for persistent sessions. When using a JMS persistent store, only available if replicated data is serialized.

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.external_write_size
metrics.description: The size of the session data written to persistent store. Applicable only for (serialized) persistent sessions. Similar to external Read Time.

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.external_write_time
metrics.description: The time (milliseconds) taken to write the session data from the persistent store. Applicable only for (serialized) persistent sessions. Similar to external Read Time.

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.invalidate_count
metrics.description: The number of sessions that were invalidated

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.life_time
metrics.description: The average session life time in milliseconds (time invalidated - time created)

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.live_count
metrics.description: The number of local sessions that are currently cached in memory from the time at which this metric is enabled.

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.no_room_for_new_session_count
metrics.description: Applies only to session in memory with AllowOverflow=false. The number of times that a request for a new session cannot be handled because it exceeds the maximum session count.

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.session_object_size
metrics.description: The size in bytes of (the serializable attributes of ) in-memory sessions. Only session objects that contain at least one serializable attribute object is counted. A session can contain some attributes that are serializable and some that are not. The size in bytes is at a session level.

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.time_since_last_activated
metrics.description: The time difference in milliseconds between previous and current access time stamps. Does not include session time out.

metrics.name: ibm_was.servlet_session.timeout_invalidation_count
metrics.description: The number of sessions that are invalidated by timeout.

metrics.name: ibm_was.thread_pools.active_count
metrics.description: The number of concurrently active threads

metrics.name: ibm_was.thread_pools.active_time
metrics.description: The average time in milliseconds the threads are in active state

metrics.name: ibm_was.thread_pools.cleared_thread_hang_count
metrics.description: The number of thread hangs cleared

metrics.name: ibm_was.thread_pools.concurrent_hung_thread_count
metrics.description: The number of concurrently hung threads

metrics.name: ibm_was.thread_pools.create_count
metrics.description: The total number of threads created

metrics.name: ibm_was.thread_pools.declared_thread_hung_count
metrics.description: The number of threads declared hung

metrics.name: ibm_was.thread_pools.destroy_count
metrics.description: The total number of threads destroyed

metrics.name: ibm_was.thread_pools.percent_maxed
metrics.description: The average percent of the time that all threads are in use

metrics.name: ibm_was.thread_pools.percent_used
metrics.description: The average percent of the pool that is in use. The value is based on the total number of configured threads in the ThreadPool and not the current pool size.

metrics.name: ibm_was.thread_pools.pool_size
metrics.description: The average number of threads in pool

serviceChecks.name: Can Connect
serviceChecks.description: Returns `CRITICAL` if the Agent cannot connect to the PerfServlet for any reason. Returns `OK` otherwise.
